title: I Took the Pinball Nudge Log to the Owner Who Left My Numbered Plunger

parts.text: I stepped into machine 7 at 8:05 p.m. and owner Hank was already using my numbered plunger. The board said: THREE BALLS. PLUNGERS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-one, arcade steward, holding a clipboard that listed our game. Hank shrugged. "Owners are the machine." I photographed the board, the booking, and his hands on my plunger. Then I asked for the nudge log. At 8:11 the arcade desk pinged why Hank's hands sat on our plunger. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The arcade desk can see Hank's hands on machine 7 during our game.

social.video_title: He left his hands on my numbered plunger — Part 1/2
social.description: Pinball, an owner on my plunger, a three-ball clock he posted. I logged the hands. Would you have asked for the nudge log?

parts.text: Hank called it tilt tests until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the plunger still. The plunger went back to my numbered cup. Hank ran a slot of their own and told the next owner atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: OWNERS ARE NOT THE MACHINE. I keep our game on a labeled card. Hank brown-bags his tilts. The machine finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Nudge log, numbered plunger, and a second line on the board. Were tilt tests ever our game?
